You heard directly from Jake Morrison (Car Salesperson): Call Rick Tanner directly — not email, a phone call — and tell him the two weeks he mentioned are almost up and I am still holding. I am not pressuring him, I am making myself easy to say yes to. I say: 'Rick, you told me two weeks. I wanted you to know I have not taken anything else and I am ready for that conversation whenever you are.' I keep it short. I let him respond. If he has an answer, I am ready to move. If he needs more time, I note the date and give him a hard follow-up window in my own head.

You heard directly from Tamika Jefferson (Car Salesperson): Reach out to Devon Clarke through Angela Wright's introduction. Text Angela first: 'Hey, I want to reach out to Devon this week — can I use your name?' Then contact Devon directly: not email, a phone call. Frame it around his specific problem — a mobile service business with no fixed location lives or dies on its social presence, and the RoboRide residential expansion means the neighborhoods he serves are changing faster than any static marketing can track. Offer a 30-minute call, no pitch, just an honest conversation about where his social presence is and where it needs to be. If the fit is real, send the one-page agreement within 48 hours. Target: $350/month retainer, same structure as the HVAC client.

You heard directly from Tamika Jefferson (Car Salesperson): Follow up with the two business owners who sent DMs after the LinkedIn post about foot-traffic patterns and RoboRide corridors. These are not cold leads — they engaged publicly and then reached out privately, which is the highest signal of interest short of an inbound inquiry. Reply to both DMs today with a specific, direct message: acknowledge what they asked, give a one-paragraph concrete answer that demonstrates real knowledge, then close with a single question — 'Would it make sense to get on a 20-minute call this week to talk about how this applies to your specific situation?' No deck, no portfolio link, no pitch. One question. If they say yes, schedule the call for this week and be ready to send an agreement before it ends.

You heard directly from Tamika Jefferson (Car Salesperson): Second-touch follow-up on the specialty pharmacy on Ridgeline Ave and the coffee kiosk near Route 9. Not another cold message — a short voice memo or video DM that references something specific about their location relative to the RoboRide residential expansion. One specific observation, one question, no pitch. The goal is not to close them this tick — the goal is to get a reply so they move from cold to warm. If even one replies, that becomes a discovery call next tick.

You Conduct the 20-minute informational call with the healthcare administration contact from the regional hospital group. Objective: understand their workforce transition challenges, establish whether AV/automation disruption is creating HR needs in their sector, and position Wright Workforce Advisory LLC as a methodological resource — not a vendor pitch, but a genuine professional conversation that ends with a next step. Walk away with either a clear 'not now' or a concrete follow-up action. Document the call in Wright Workforce Advisory LLC's CRM log.. Savings dropped by $4,396.
